A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAP research. Their text, figures, tables and equations support comparison. V1 has no separate appendix; v2's supplementary material preserves several 3D experiments previously in the main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet and point-cloud experiments, including pretraining comparisons, component ablations, few-shot classification and part segmentation.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments in the main text and supplement and adds ImageNet comparison results and ADE20K/COCO transfer evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain random masking, the interleaved Mamba-Transformer backbone, row-wise Transformer decoding and normalized-pixel MSE reconstruction. HybridMH/HybridMT3D are renamed HybridNet. The new probabilistic description and MambaVision experiments do not establish a changed MAP procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation and COCO 2017 object detection and instance segmentation in Section 5.2, substantially extending image-task coverage. ImageNet, ShapeNet pretraining, ModelNet40 including few-shot classification, ScanObjectNN and ShapeNetPart remain represented, with several 3D evaluations relocated to the supplement.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds MambaR-B+MAE and MambaR-B+AR comparisons and includes ViT-B+AR, previously reported in the pilot study. New transfer tables compare against DeepLab v3+, UperNet configurations and DeiT/Vim backbones. The existing ImageNet and 3D comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New transfer protocols introduce UperNet with 512×512 images and validation mIoU on ADE20K, and box/mask AP on COCO. MAP is also evaluated on MambaVision-B/L configurations. Existing ImageNet and 3D training budgets remain unchanged. The exact COCO framework is unclear: Section 5.2 names ViTDet, whereas Table 10 names Cascade Mask R-CNN.

E4.justification: V1's hybrid-ratio sensitivity study comparing 3:1, 1:3 and 2:2 mixtures disappears, including Table 9 and its discussion. The scanning-order, masking-ratio, masking-pattern, layer-placement, decoder-mask and reconstruction-loss ablations remain, sometimes renumbered.

E5.justification: Existing few-shot and baseline ± reporting is retained, including identical few-shot entries in v1 Table 11 and v2 Table 12. V2 introduces no seed information, repetition counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; its new benchmark results use point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds MambaVision-B/L+MAP accuracies of 84.9/86.4 and MambaR-B+MAE/AR accuracies of 83.1/83.7. New transfer tables report HybridNet-S+MAP at 46.9 ADE20K mIoU and HybridNet-Ti+MAP at 46.4 box AP/39.8 mask AP on COCO. Matched existing ImageNet and 3D scores remain unchanged; alternative hybrid-ratio results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4 adds Equations 1–5 defining image rows, tokens and masked subsets, a conditional probability factorization, and a masked-token negative log-likelihood objective. V1 describes MAP procedurally without this mathematical formulation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1's abstract highlights the layer-placement finding and asserts state-of-the-art performance for both pure Mamba and hybrid backbones. V2 restricts that abstract assertion to hybrids and explicitly places hybrid-architecture design outside its scope. The central contribution of unified MAP pretraining and its 2D/3D effectiveness remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds a limitation that MAP hybrids struggle to surpass MAE-pretrained Transformers under the same settings. It explains the Transformer decoder choice and interprets retained resolution/model-size results through context length and scaling. The main local-feature/context explanation remains; the hybrid-ratio interpretation and speculative diffusion-decoder-capacity explanation are removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code/checkpoint repository link and specifies that few-shot accuracy is reported without voting. It omits v1's dataset-specific 3D fine-tuning augmentations and explicit 3D masking-ratio disclosure. These are documentation changes, without evidence that the retained experiments used different settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds MaskMamba, LongLLaVA and transfer-task references, supplies citations for already listed IDPT and Point-M2AE comparisons, and removes Hamilton's state-space reference. Related work now explicitly distinguishes MAP's masking/local reconstruction from ARM and discusses ARM's relationship to scanning-order consistency.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory framing and conclusion are substantially rewritten around hybrid pretraining. Section 4 is reorganized into a backbone preliminary and method overview, explanations are expanded, and much of the 3D discussion moves into a supplement. Hybrid backbone terminology is standardized as HybridNet.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, restacks Figure 1 and compresses Table 8 from a full-page display into one column. V1's combined 3D tables are split across main-text and supplementary tables. The AR masking schematic and hybrid-ratio table disappear, while two transfer-result tables are added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, MambaVision tests and image dense-prediction evaluations strengthen evidence for MAP's applicability beyond the custom hybrid, while MambaR-B controls improve pretraining comparisons. Code/checkpoint access information also helps reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of the ratio study and some 3D settings, plus inconsistent COCO framework descriptions, yielding a limited net improvement.
